chunks: And from them both with this chain of narration from Abu Sa'id al-'Usfuri, from Hammad ibn Ayyub, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'My son will be buried in a land known as Karbala. It is the spot where the Dome of Islam was, from which Allah saved the believers who believed with Noah during the Flood.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الطُّوفَانِ: The Flood, referring to the biblical/Quranic flood during the time of Prophet Noah
key_terms.قُبَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The Dome of Islam, a metaphorical or literal structure signifying the preservation of faith
key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءُ: Karbala, a city in Iraq known as the burial place of Imam al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Karbala in Shia tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* establishes Karbala not merely as a burial site but as the 'Dome of Islam' (Qubbat al-Islam), a locus of divine salvation where the faithful were preserved during the Flood. By linking Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom to the era of Noah, Shia scholarship elevates his sacrifice to a primordial event of cosmic deliverance, reinforcing the spiritual centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in Islamic history.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. And from them both with this chain of narration from Abu Sa'id al-'Usfuri, from Hammad ibn Ayyub, from Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.), from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir al-Mu'minin (a.s.), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (sw) said, 'My son will be buried in a land known as Karbala. It is the blessed spot where the Dome of Islam stands, from which Allah saved the believers who believed with Noah during the Flood.'"
